items.stem: During the instruction cycle, which step places the address of the next instruction onto the memory bus so it can be retrieved?

options.text: The fetch step, which uses the program counter to address memory
options.rationale: Correct: fetch uses the program counter to read the next instruction from memory.

options.text: The execute step, after the ALU computes a result
options.rationale: Execute performs the operation; the instruction has already been fetched.

options.text: The decode step, which only interprets the opcode
options.rationale: Decode interprets the fetched instruction; it does not fetch it.

options.text: The write-back step, which stores results to registers
options.rationale: Write-back stores results; it does not fetch instructions.

items.explanation: Correct: fetch uses the program counter to read the next instruction from memory.

items.stem: Which TWO properties of a program improve the hit rate of a CPU cache? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Temporal locality, where recently used data is reused soon
options.rationale: Correct: reused data stays resident in cache, raising the hit rate.

options.text: Spatial locality, where nearby addresses are accessed together
options.rationale: Correct: fetching a cache line serves neighbouring accesses.

options.text: A larger working set than the cache capacity
options.rationale: A working set exceeding capacity causes evictions and lowers the hit rate.

options.text: Purely random access across a huge address range
options.rationale: Random wide access defeats both temporal and spatial locality.

items.explanation: Correct: reused data stays resident in cache, raising the hit rate.

items.stem: A workload is 75% parallelisable. By Amdahl's law, what is the maximum speedup with unlimited processors?

options.text: 4x, because the serial 25% bounds the speedup to 1/0.25
options.rationale: Correct: the serial fraction 0.25 limits speedup to 1/0.25 = 4x.

options.text: Unlimited, because all work can eventually be parallelised
options.rationale: The serial 25% can never be parallelised, so speedup is bounded.

options.text: 1.33x, because only the serial part speeds up
options.rationale: The parallel part speeds up; the serial part is the bound.
Amdahl's law bounds speedup by the inverse of the serial fraction.

items.explanation: Correct: the serial fraction 0.25 limits speedup to 1/0.25 = 4x.
